pointers.sentence: A view is defined by how it is used, and the use is a single line of `BaseHandler._get_response`, or of its asynchronous twin under ASGI: the callable that the resolver returned is called with the request, then the positional arguments, then the keyword arguments (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler._get_response`).

The keyword arguments are what the path's parameters captured, together with any extra arguments written in the URLconf after the view, or after an `include` on the way to it (`django/urls/resolvers.py:URLPattern.resolve`, `django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver.resolve`).

The system checks that do try a view's signature against stand-in arguments are for views Django calls on its own account: the error views ([The error views](errors.md#found-through-the-urlconf-called-like-a-view)) and the view named by `settings.CSRF_FAILURE_VIEW` (`django/core/checks/urls.py:check_custom_error_handlers`, `django/core/checks/security/csrf.py:check_csrf_failure_view`).

`path` and `re_path` take whatever is callable and keep it as `URLPattern.callback` (`django/urls/conf.py:_path`).
The resolver hands each back as it was given, an *Almanac* and a `functools.partial` (`django/urls/resolvers.py:URLPattern.resolve`).

For a subclass of `View` the system check `"urls.E009"` reports the mistake ([The URL checks, and listing the patterns](../urls/checks.md#the-four-checks-tagged-urls)), and a request routed to it all the same ordinarily ends as a 500: the handler calls the class with the request, and `View.__init__`, which takes keyword arguments only, raises a `TypeError` (`django/urls/resolvers.py:URLPattern._check_callback`, `django/views/generic/base.py:View.__init__`).

Each raises a `ValueError` whose message names the view (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.check_response`).

The check does not follow `"view_class"`, which would have named the class; [`View.as_view` and dispatch](as-view.md) tells that `as_view` leaves the function's name alone and records the class there instead (`django/views/generic/base.py:View.as_view`).

With no middleware the first such use is in `BaseHandler.get_response`, outside the chain and its exception handling, so the `AttributeError` leaves the handler, and what the client then gets is the server's to decide (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.get_response`, `django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIHandler.__call__`).

With `CommonMiddleware` alone installed, that middleware's `process_response` is the first to touch the object, the failure happens inside the chain, and the client gets an ordinary 500 (`django/middleware/common.py:CommonMiddleware.process_response`).

For a view, raising is a second way of answering: the handler ordinarily turns an exception that no `process_exception` hook answers into a response chosen by its class ([How an exception becomes a response](../handlers/exceptions.md)) (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:response_for_exception`).

So the view carries a mark, an attribute set by a decorator, by `as_view`, or by the admin site for its own views, which the code that needs to know looks for with `getattr` and a default, or with `hasattr` (`django/middleware/csrf.py:CsrfViewMiddleware.process_view`, `django/urls/resolvers.py:ResolverMatch.__init__`).

It does when each decorator outside copies the wrapped function's attributes onto its own wrapper, which `functools.wraps` does, and every wrapper made in `django/views/decorators/` is passed through it.

`as_view` has the same problem with a class and solves it for one method: it copies the attributes added to `dispatch` onto the function it returns ([Decorating a class: `method_decorator`](method-decorator.md)) (`django/views/generic/base.py:View.as_view`).

Three of them are the message of `check_response`; the dotted path that `ResolverMatch` keeps, which a debug page prints (`django/views/debug.py:get_caller`); and `URLPattern.lookup_str`, against which the admin's documentation checks a dotted name before it imports a view ([Reversing a name](../urls/reversing.md#the-tables)) (`django/urls/resolvers.py:URLPattern.lookup_str`).
